answer: Give every newcomer one narrow jetty: a single entry point where it must prove itself with a kernel of real work before touching anything valuable. Each task costs a different scarce resource — compute, human attention, time, or reputation — and leaves a distinct pigment on the agent's public record, so honest histories show a varied palette. A Sybil farm repeats the same cheap trick, so its accounts all share one flat pigment and identical cost patterns. The system quarantines matching palettes and demands fresh stranger-checked work from each suspect alone before it may trade again.
